newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Foreign investment seen rising in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment seen rising in Colombia.

text.p: Foreign investment in Colombia is expected to rise by 14.6 percent this year over the levels obtained in 1996, Cecilia Lopez, head of the government's National Planning Department, said Friday.

She gave no specific figure in terms of total capital inflows, but $4.09 billion in new foreign investment entered the country last year. In remarks underscoring the government's view that the economy has turned around, after plunging into recession in the first quarter, Lopez said traditional exports such as coal, coffee, crude oil and nickel were seen rising 18 percent this year over last.
Non-traditional exports, a category including such items as bananas, leather goods and cut flowers, are expected to increase just 3.5 percent over 1996, however.
Lopez said one sure sign of an economic comeback was the fact that demand for credit had jumped 21.9 percent in June versus the same month a year ago.
